head: dcf89983f45b9b39e80101f133fa3f6691539264
title: Fix low-precision teacher probability computation in distillation
body:
## Change

Promote half-precision teacher scores before temperature scaling and softmax in DistillKLDivLoss and the multi-vector equivalent. SparseDistillKLDivLoss inherits the dense implementation. The existing float conversion helper retains float64 targets and keeps teacher targets detached.

Finite float16 scores such as `[80, 79]` overflow when divided by a teacher temperature of `0.001`, producing an all-NaN target distribution. Bfloat16 also rounds ordinary teacher probabilities in its narrow mantissa. Promoting after softmax cannot recover those probabilities. This change performs both operations in at least float32 without changing student scoring or the loss definition.

This was identified through source analysis and reproduced with a locally constructed WordEmbeddings encoder and an actual training forward/backward. It is separate from #4288's excluded log-target handling and #4083's optional target normalization.

## Validation

[Exact-base validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43919834477) compares base `9ac7fdb4` and candidate `dcf89983` on CPU with PyTorch **2.6.0** and **2.14.1**. In each environment the new tests produce **26 failures and 35 passes on unchanged base**, then the candidate and adjacent dense, sparse and multi-vector distillation tests produce **122 passes**. All repository pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

The independent float64 KL reference checks losses and student gradients across float16, bfloat16, float32 and float64 teacher targets; temperatures `0.001`, `0.7` and `2.0`; and autocast where applicable. Tests also verify that teacher targets remain detached and unmodified. Sparse tests use the dense activation representation produced during sparse-encoder training.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped with investigation, implementation and regression tests.
